body: `output.trim()` can still contain embedded newlines if stdout includes additional lines (e.g., warnings/logging), and the current check only validates the first character. That would incorrectly accept a multi-line string and propagate newlines into the rendered prompt version. Consider parsing only the first non-empty line (or first token) and validating that single-line value (e.g., no whitespace) before returning it; also add a unit test covering a multi-line stdout starting with a digit to prevent regressions.
